findings.evidence: DOM order: step3, step2, step1. CSS order property: order:3, order:2, order:1. Visual reading order: Choose a plan (step1) -> Enter payment details (step2) -> Confirm your order (step3). Screen reader DOM order: Confirm your order -> Enter payment details -> Choose a plan.
findings.violation: Checkout workflow sequence is reversed in DOM order compared to visual order and the logical task sequence. A screen reader user would hear steps in reverse (confirm, pay, choose) while a sighted user sees them in forward sequence (choose, pay, confirm), breaking the meaningful sequence required by the criterion.
findings.fix: Reorder the DOM elements to match the visual order, or remove the CSS order property and rely on source order. The correct DOM sequence should be step1 (Choose a plan), step2 (Enter payment details), step3 (Confirm your order).

findings.evidence: Label element with style='color:#cc0000' displays phone label in red. No other visual signal present: no asterisk character, no 'required' text, no icon, no other distinguishing marker.
findings.violation: The required status of the phone field is indicated only through color (red), with no accompanying text, icon, or other non-color signal. Color-blind users cannot distinguish this field from optional fields.
findings.fix: Add a visible text indicator such as an asterisk after the label text, or add the word 'required' to the label, or use an icon in addition to the color, so the required status is conveyed through means other than color alone.

findings.location: Section 3 form, promo code field and error message (input id=promo, span id=s3-form-promo-error)
findings.evidence: Input element has aria-invalid='true'. Associated error text reads 'Error.' - a single word with a period, providing no information about which field is wrong or what is wrong with it.
findings.violation: The error message is too generic. It does not identify the specific item in error (though proximity to the field suggests it) nor does it describe what is wrong with the input, leaving users unable to correct the problem.
findings.fix: Replace the generic 'Error.' message with a specific description of the problem, such as 'Invalid promo code format' or 'Promo code not found'. Also add aria-describedby on the input field to programmatically associate it with the error message span.

findings.evidence: Div element with class='icon-delete' containing an img with src='/img/trash-icon.svg' alt=''. The div has no role attribute, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no accessible name of any kind, and no visible text content that would serve as a label.
findings.violation: The custom control element exposes no programmatic role (e.g., button, toolbar button), no accessible name conveying its purpose, and no state information. A screen reader user cannot detect this control exists, cannot determine what it does, and cannot activate it.
findings.fix: Add role='button' to the div element and add an accessible name via aria-label='Delete' or similar descriptive text. Ensure the control is keyboard-accessible via a click handler that responds to Enter and Space keys, or convert it to a native button element with visible text or aria-label.
